Kameda, by contrast, was cremated in accordance with the ordinary custom for kings. Neither cremation was an exceptional victory honor nor was burial inherently disgraceful. The revealing difference was that Umio’s side could no longer determine or perform its own funeral rites. People took that loss of control as evidence that Umio’s faction had been defeated, so they judged Umio the likely loser despite his body remaining intact."}
